one_liner: Builds and runs the systems that clean up what industry and cities produce.
job_roles: Environmental Engineer | Water & Wastewater Treatment Engineer | Air Quality Engineer | Solid Waste Management Engineer | ETP & STP Operations Engineer | Environmental Compliance Engineer | Contaminated Site Remediation Specialist | Industrial Hygiene & Emissions Engineer
entrance_exams: JEE Main | GATE | State engineering entrance examinations
self_emp_route: An independent environmental consultancy doing consents, monitoring and compliance reporting for small industry. A common step after eight to ten years, and it depends on relationships with the State Pollution Control Board.
ai_reason: Low exposure and protected by physical infrastructure. A treatment plant is pumps, blowers and biology that must be kept alive, and ETP & STP Operations Engineer is nearly untouched. Environmental Compliance Engineer carries the exposure - consent applications, returns and standard reports are documentation work that generates well - but the signature on a statutory return still belongs to a person the board can act against.
role_spread: [ETP & STP Operations Engineer] higher: bodily, conscientiousness, attention_span / lower: openness || [Environmental Compliance Engineer] higher: verbal, logical, conscientiousness / lower: bodily
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Physics and Mathematics. Chemistry is NOT compulsory - JEE Main Paper 1 accepts Chemistry, Biology, Biotechnology or a technical vocational subject as the third. -> entrance_exam: JEE Main, a state engineering entrance, or a private university entrance. -> degree: B.Tech in Environmental Engineering, or Civil or Chemical Engineering with an environmental specialisation. -> work: Environmental consultancy, an industrial EHS department, a water or waste utility, or an EPC contractor building treatment plants.
nuances: [demand_signal] Moderate and regulation-driven rather than market-driven, which makes it unusually predictable. Every industrial unit needs consent to operate and every city needs sewage treated, so demand tracks enforcement capacity rather than the economy. Where enforcement is weak, so is hiring. || [professional_sector] Promised here from Sector 2 and it belongs here on the substitution test, narrowly. Remove the environment and a treatment plant engineer is a process engineer - but the object of concern is what happens to the discharge after it leaves the fence, and that is not a manufacturing question.

one_liner: Measures what is happening to air, water, soil and ecosystems, and what a project will do.
job_roles: Environmental Scientist | EIA Consultant | Environmental Monitoring Analyst | Air Quality Analyst | Water Quality Analyst | Soil & Groundwater Scientist | Ecotoxicologist | Environmental Laboratory Analyst | Biodiversity Assessment Specialist
entrance_exams: CUET UG | CUET PG | GATE (Ecology and Evolution) | NABET/QCI EIA accreditation
self_emp_route: Independent consultancy once NABET-accredited, which is the credential that lets you sign reports rather than prepare them for someone else's signature.
ai_reason: Low exposure, protected by sampling. Somebody has to be at the outfall with a bottle and at the stack with a probe, and Environmental Monitoring Analyst and Biodiversity Assessment Specialist are field jobs. EIA Consultant carries the real exposure: an EIA report is a long document assembled to a template from monitoring data, and much of the drafting is generatable. The accreditation and the public hearing are what a model cannot supply.
role_spread: [EIA Consultant] higher: verbal, reasoning, conscientiousness / lower: bodily || [Environmental Laboratory Analyst, Environmental Monitoring Analyst] higher: attention_span, conscientiousness, logical / lower: confidence || [Biodiversity Assessment Specialist] higher: naturalistic, attention_span, bodily / lower: extraversion
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Science stream in practice; Biology or Chemistry are the usual routes and neither is formally required for every programme. -> degree: BSc in Environmental Science, or any science degree followed by an MSc in Environmental Science. -> masters: MSc is effectively the entry qualification for anything beyond laboratory analysis. -> accreditation: For EIA work, NABET/QCI accreditation as a Functional Area Expert or EIA Coordinator - this is what lets you sign a report. -> work: Environmental consultancy, a pollution control board, an industrial EHS team, a research institute or an NGO.
nuances: [licensing_body] Null, but NOT unconstrained. NABET accreditation under the Quality Council of India determines who may sign an Environmental Impact Assessment report, which is a genuine commercial gate created by the environmental clearance process rather than by a professions statute. It is closer to an auditor's empanelment than to a licence. || [demand_signal] Moderate. The volume of work follows the environmental clearance pipeline - infrastructure, mining and industrial projects - so it moves with capital investment cycles rather than with environmental need.

one_liner: Turns satellite imagery and maps into answers about land, water, forests and cities.
job_roles: GIS Analyst | Remote Sensing Analyst | Cartographer | Geospatial Data Scientist | Photogrammetrist | Drone Survey Analyst | Spatial Database Administrator | Land Records Digitisation Specialist | Urban Mapping Analyst
entrance_exams: CUET PG | GATE (Geomatics) | IIRS and state remote sensing centre courses
self_emp_route: Independent geospatial services - drone survey, mapping and land records work for local bodies and developers. Owning a survey drone changes the economics, and the operator needs a DGCA Remote Pilot Certificate.
ai_reason: The most exposed profession in this sector. Automated feature extraction, change detection and classification from satellite imagery are exactly what computer vision does, and Cartographer and much routine GIS Analyst work is already substantially automated. What survives is at both ends: Drone Survey Analyst because someone must fly and ground-truth, and Geospatial Data Scientist because building the models is the work rather than the casualty. Land Records Digitisation Specialist is protected for an unglamorous reason - the source documents are handwritten, disputed and legally consequential.
role_spread: [Geospatial Data Scientist] higher: logical, reasoning, attention_span / lower: bodily || [Land Records Digitisation Specialist] higher: conscientiousness, attention_span, verbal / lower: openness || [Drone Survey Analyst] higher: spatial, bodily, logical / lower: verbal
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream. Mathematics and Geography both help. -> degree: Geography, geology, environmental science, civil engineering, computer science or planning - all are normal routes in. -> specialisation: A postgraduate diploma or MSc in GIS and Remote Sensing, or demonstrable skill with QGIS, ArcGIS, Google Earth Engine and Python. -> work: Government mapping and land records programmes, ISRO and state remote sensing centres, urban planning bodies, environmental consultancies, or private geospatial firms.
nuances: [industrial_sectors] Promised here from Sector 3 rather than kept with the sciences. The method is technical and could sit almost anywhere; the object of concern is land, water and ecosystems, which is this sector. The tagging to IT-ITES and EXT-GOVT is the honest signal that a GIS analyst's employer is very often neither environmental nor scientific. || [demand_signal] Moderate, and unusually policy-anchored: the largest single driver in India is government land records digitisation and urban mapping under national programmes, not private-sector demand.

one_liner: Protects forests and wildlife - as a government officer, a researcher, or with communities.
job_roles: Indian Forest Service Officer | Forest Range Officer | Forester | Forest Guard | Wildlife Biologist | Conservation Project Officer | Wildlife Veterinarian Assistant | Eco-development & Community Forestry Officer | Nature Interpretation Guide | Anti-Poaching Watcher
entrance_exams: UPSC Indian Forest Service Examination | State Forest Service examinations | State Forest Range Officer and Forest Guard recruitment
ai_reason: Among the least exposed professions in the dataset. The work is being physically present in a forest - patrolling, identifying, seizing, negotiating - and a Range Officer's statutory powers require a person to exercise them. Wildlife Biologist carries the only real exposure, through automated species identification from camera trap images, which has changed the method rather than the job.
role_spread: [Indian Forest Service Officer, Forest Range Officer] higher: confidence, conscientiousness, logical / lower: agreeableness || [Wildlife Biologist] higher: naturalistic, reasoning, attention_span / lower: confidence || [Forest Guard, Anti-Poaching Watcher] higher: bodily, attention_span / lower: verbal, emotional_stability || [Eco-development & Community Forestry Officer, Nature Interpretation Guide] higher: extraversion, agreeableness, verbal, emotional_stability / lower: -
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Science stream for the IFS route - the degree must include a listed science, or be in agriculture, forestry or engineering. -> degree: BSc in a science, forestry, agriculture or engineering. For research, an MSc in Wildlife Science or Ecology. -> entrance_exam: UPSC Indian Forest Service for the All-India cadre; state forest service and Range Officer examinations for the far larger state cadres. -> training: Indira Gandhi National Forest Academy for IFS officers, or a state forest training institute. -> work: Forest department, a protected area, a research institute, or a conservation NGO.
nuances: [economics] One figure across two very different careers, and the record should be read with that in mind. An IFS officer enters on a Group A pay scale with housing and a pension; a Forest Guard is increasingly hired on contract or daily wage and earns a fraction of it, while doing the patrolling that carries the physical risk. The mid_career figure describes the officer end. This is the same bimodal problem as School Teacher in Sector 12 and MBBS cost in Sector 4. || [ai_exposure] legal_accountability is true with no licensing body, on the statutory-office precedent used for District Magistrate and Police Officer in Sector 7. A Forest Range Officer exercises powers of search, seizure and prosecution under the Indian Forest Act and the Wild Life (Protection) Act, and is personally answerable for their exercise. || [self_employment] Rare, and unusually clearly so. Forest protection authority derives entirely from statutory office - there is no independent version. The conservation NGO and research roles are employed too. Nature Interpretation Guide is the single exception and is a tourism livelihood rather than a conservation career. || [demand_signal] Low in the sense that matters: 150 IFS posts a year nationally, and state Range Officer recruitment is intermittent. The Forest Guard cadre is far larger and is increasingly filled on contract and daily wage rather than as permanent posts.

one_liner: Measures and reports what a company does to the environment and society, to a legal standard.
job_roles: Sustainability Analyst | ESG Reporting Specialist | Carbon Accounting Analyst | Energy Auditor | Sustainability Consultant | ESG Assurance Associate | Climate Disclosure Analyst | Supply Chain Sustainability Analyst | Green Building Consultant
entrance_exams: CAT | CUET PG | Sustainability and GHG accounting certifications
self_emp_route: Independent sustainability and energy audit consultancy, which is a real market because BRSR Core requires third-party assurance and small companies need help preparing to be assured.
ai_reason: Substantially exposed, and it is worth being blunt because this profession is currently fashionable. ESG Reporting Specialist, Climate Disclosure Analyst and Carbon Accounting Analyst do work that is largely data collection, conversion against published emission factors, and narrative assembly to a template - which is close to a canonical automation target. What is protected is Energy Auditor and Green Building Consultant, because those require walking a site, and ESG Assurance Associate, because assurance requires a firm to put its name to an opinion.
role_spread: [Energy Auditor, Green Building Consultant] higher: logical, spatial, bodily / lower: verbal || [ESG Assurance Associate] higher: conscientiousness, attention_span, logical / lower: openness
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream. -> degree: Environmental science, engineering, commerce or economics. This profession recruits from all four and the commerce route is growing fastest because the work is reporting. -> certification: Optional but valued: BEE Certified Energy Auditor, GHG accounting certifications, or a sustainability master's. -> work: A listed company's sustainability team, an accountancy or consulting firm's ESG practice, an assurance provider, or a rating agency.
nuances: [demand_signal] High, and unusually well explained by a single regulation. SEBI's BRSR made sustainability reporting mandatory for the top 1,000 listed companies from FY 2022-23, and BRSR Core extends third-party assurance to all of them by FY 2026-27. That is a compliance deadline creating jobs, which is a far more reliable demand signal than corporate enthusiasm. || [ai_exposure] The highest-paid profession in this sector is also among its most exposed, and those two facts are related: the work pays well because it is newly mandatory, and it is exposed because most of it is structured data assembly. A student entering it should aim at the assurance and audit end rather than the reporting end.

one_liner: Gets solar and wind projects built and running - siting, resource, permits, performance.
job_roles: Solar Project Developer | Wind Resource Analyst | Renewable Energy Project Manager | Solar Plant Performance Analyst | Grid Integration Analyst | Renewable Energy Site Engineer | Battery Storage Analyst | Rooftop Solar Consultant | Power Purchase Agreement Analyst
self_emp_route: Rooftop solar installation and EPC on own account, which is a genuine small-business route with modest capital, or independent technical advisory to lenders and developers after a decade.
ai_reason: Moderate exposure concentrated on the analytical roles. Wind Resource Analyst, Solar Plant Performance Analyst and Battery Storage Analyst work on time-series modelling, which is directly automatable and already heavily software-mediated. Renewable Energy Site Engineer and Rooftop Solar Consultant are protected - one by being on a construction site in the desert, the other by having to persuade a housing society committee.
role_spread: [Wind Resource Analyst, Solar Plant Performance Analyst] higher: logical, reasoning, attention_span / lower: extraversion || [Rooftop Solar Consultant] higher: extraversion, verbal, confidence / lower: logical || [Renewable Energy Site Engineer] higher: bodily, spatial, conscientiousness / lower: verbal
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Physics and Mathematics for the engineering route; any stream for the commercial and consulting roles. -> degree: Electrical, mechanical or energy engineering, or an economics or commerce degree for the project finance and PPA side. -> work: A developer, an EPC contractor, a consultancy, or a state renewable energy development agency. -> specialisation: Development, resource assessment, operations or offtake. These pay very differently and are hard to move between.
nuances: [demand_signal] High, and among the best-founded demand signals in this dataset because it rests on installed capacity targets and on projects with financing already closed - not on sentiment. The caveat is geographic: development and operations jobs are in Rajasthan, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka. || [professional_sector] Solar and wind ENGINEERING sits in Sector 2 - an electrical engineer is an electrical engineer, and Solar Panel Technician was merged into Electrician there on exactly that test. What is here is the project layer: siting, resource, permits, offtake and performance, where the object of concern is the energy transition rather than the machine.

one_liner: Collects, sorts and disposes of what cities throw away, and keeps the sewers running.
job_roles: Sanitation Worker | Waste Collection Worker | Waste Sorter & Segregator | Sewer & Septic Tank Worker | Material Recovery Facility Operator | Composting Unit Operator | Sanitation Supervisor | Waste Picker | Sanitation Entrepreneur (Mechanised Cleaning) | Street Sweeper | Sewer Sweeper
self_emp_route: Owning mechanised desludging or collection equipment and contracting to urban local bodies. This is what the NAMASTE scheme's capital support exists to fund, and it is the difference between doing this work and running it.
ai_reason: Almost unexposed by AI, and that is the least important thing about the risk in this profession. The technology that matters here is not artificial intelligence but MECHANISATION - suction desludging machines, sewer robots and material recovery equipment - which is policy's declared answer to the deaths and which would displace exactly the manual roles it protects. Sanitation Supervisor and Material Recovery Facility Operator are the roles that survive mechanisation.
role_spread: [Sanitation Entrepreneur (Mechanised Cleaning)] higher: confidence, logical, conscientiousness / lower: bodily || [Material Recovery Facility Operator, Composting Unit Operator] higher: logical, attention_span, conscientiousness, emotional_stability / lower: - || [Sewer & Septic Tank Worker] higher: bodily / lower: verbal, openness, emotional_stability
path_to_entry: class_11_12: None. This work is entered without schooling and overwhelmingly by people from Scheduled Caste communities. -> profiling: Profiling under the NAMASTE scheme for sewer and septic tank workers, which brings PPE, health insurance and training. -> work: Urban local body, a private sanitation contractor, or informal waste picking. Most is contract or daily wage rather than municipal employment. -> route_out: Capital subsidy under NAMASTE to become a sanitation entrepreneur operating mechanised equipment - the scheme's own stated objective, and the only documented route out.
review_reason: Three things are owed. No sourced wage figure exists for Indian sanitation workers, municipal or contract. No figure exists for what a NAMASTE-supported sanitation entrepreneur earns, which is the only documented route out of manual work. And a presentation decision is needed that the schema cannot make: how a recommender should surface an occupation that is large, lawful in part, lethal in part, and caste-bound in practice - it should almost certainly never be RECOMMENDED, only described.
nuances: [demand_signal] High and permanent - every city generates waste daily - but this is demand for labour under conditions the law has already declared unacceptable. The Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers Act 2013 bans manual handling of human excreta, and about 38,000 sewer and septic tank workers had been profiled under NAMASTE by September 2024 against a ministry estimate of around 100,000 in urban India. || [economics] Fails the compensation filter, and listing this profession is a deliberate decision rather than an oversight. It is one of the largest occupations in urban India, it is overwhelmingly done by Scheduled Caste workers on contract or daily wage, and leaving it out would let the taxonomy present Indian work as cleaner than it is. The record names the route out - mechanised sanitation entrepreneurship - because the scheme that funds it is the honest answer to the question a student would ask. || [job_roles] Sewer & Septic Tank Worker is listed and must be read with its role_spread entry. Entering a sewer or septic tank manually is unlawful and continues to kill workers in India each year. It is recorded so that the hazard is visible in the data, not because it is a career anyone should be routed toward.

one_liner: Plans for floods, cyclones, heat and earthquakes before they happen, and coordinates after.
job_roles: Disaster Management Officer | Emergency Operations Coordinator | Climate Risk & Vulnerability Analyst | Hazard Mapping Specialist | Early Warning Systems Analyst | Relief & Rehabilitation Coordinator | Heat Action Plan Coordinator | Community Preparedness Trainer
entrance_exams: CUET PG | UPSC Civil Services Examination | State public service commissions
self_emp_route: Independent climate risk and resilience advisory to cities, lenders and companies. Growing, because climate risk disclosure is becoming a financial requirement rather than a public-sector one.
ai_reason: Moderate exposure on the analytical half. Hazard Mapping Specialist and Early Warning Systems Analyst work with models and geospatial data that are increasingly automated, and forecasting itself is a machine learning success story. Emergency Operations Coordinator and Community Preparedness Trainer are protected entirely - coordinating a response and persuading a village to evacuate are things done by a person who is there.
role_spread: [Relief & Rehabilitation Coordinator, Emergency Operations Coordinator] higher: confidence, extraversion / lower: openness, emotional_stability || [Climate Risk & Vulnerability Analyst, Hazard Mapping Specialist] higher: logical, spatial, reasoning / lower: extraversion
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream. -> degree: Geography, geology, civil engineering, environmental science, planning or social work - all are routes in. -> specialisation: A master's in disaster management, climate science or urban planning; or entry through the development sector. -> work: State or district disaster management authority, a municipal resilience cell, a humanitarian agency, or a consultancy advising cities and lenders on climate risk.
nuances: [demand_signal] Moderate, and it is a profession whose need and whose funded posts are badly mismatched. India's exposure to flood, cyclone and extreme heat is rising and measurable; the number of specialist posts is small, and the senior ones are usually filled by generalist administrative officers rather than by specialists. || [demand_signal] Pathway is 'any' because climate risk analysis has become a financial-sector skill internationally - lenders and insurers now require it - which gives this profession an unusual escape route from India's thin public-sector demand.
